chapter: Later bands, Joe Turner and records
title: His own Rinky Dinks band with Punch Miller
summary: Herman Sherman, his sons and Punch Miller in his band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now, who did you have in your own violin? I know I mentioned Rankin Dixon. Did you tell me who you used in your own violin?
Well, I had Herman Sherman. All right. My two sons. I would use a violin. And I would use a violin. On his violin. And that dial. Mm-hmm.
What was Herman Sherman playing? Alto saxophone. And then the violin would be playing the... Tenor saxophone. And the ounce? On the trumpet. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Has he lost any weight?
No, he saw him. Oh, yes, sir. He's been out there. He's been out there. Oh, yeah, I see. He was out. He just pulled off when he said it came out. Mm-hmm.
Did you know Punch Miller here in town? When he was here in the 20s?
Oh, Punch came here around 58. Mm-hmm. And Punch told me, he said that Punch was stopping down at Page Hotel.

And Punch... I met Punch. I met Punch. Punch said that New Orleans musician... I met him by Papa John Sharp. Yeah. And he said that New Orleans musician didn't have much fun. And so I put him with the rink-a-dinks. Oh, yeah. I put Punch with me. Mm-hmm. And Punch stayed with me a long time. He was playing first trumpet and my son was playing second trumpet on the Punch. I had the band in with Punch and Herman Cham was still there and myself.
What's he like? He plays everything, huh?

Well, he plays drums and piano and trumpet. And he studied that in school. And he knew the other instruments, knew the fingering, you know, and positions on the other instruments. And some of them he'd play. And he was playing that. He's a natural talent.
